sentences.text: The gist of the prosecution case is that the accused No.1 married CW-1 on 01-03- 2017.
At the time of marriage, the accused have demanded and taken dowry from complainant and her family.

After marriage,
accused have subjected CW-2 to mental and physical cruelty by quarreling with her for petty matters, abusing her in filthy language, assaulted her with hands and sent her out of the house without any reason within three months of marriage.
The accused took loan of Rs.Ten lakhs in the name of CW-1 and did not repay the same, harassed her for giving birth to a female child.

During March, 2021 the accused have quarreled with CW-1 for additional dowry, snatched her mangalasutra, assaulted her and sent her out of the house and thus subjected CW-1 to physical and mental cruelty.
Based on the said information, a case in Cr.No.89/2024 came to be registered against the accused for the aforesaid offences.

After completion of the investigation, the P.S.I.
Basavanagudi Women P.S. has filed chargesheet against accused for the aforesaid offences.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took cognizance of the alleged offences.
Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons, accused entered appearance and were enlarged on bail.

The prosecution papers was furnished to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.
 4.

Before framing charge an opportunity of being heard was Smt Jayalaxmi vs Suresh B K on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196355082/
2 provided to the accused No.1 after hearing him and the prosecution and as there was sufficient materials, the charge for the aforesaid offences was framed and same was read over to the accused in the language known to him, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

sentences.text: The plea of the accused was recorded.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution has examined PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.3 documents.
As there were no any incriminating circumstances in the evidence against  4  C.C.No.39164/2024 the accused, the statement of accused as required U/s.313 of Cr.P.C., is dispensed with.
6. Heard arguments on both the sides.
I have Perused the materials on record.

7. The following points arise for my determination:-
 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that the accused person caused physical and  mental cruelty to the complainant in demand of dowry  abused, assaulted and threatened her and thereby  accused have committed the offences punishable U/s.
 498A, 323 of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.?
 2) what order?
 8. My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 ........In the Negative.
Point No.2........

As per final order, for the following:-
 REASONS  9. POINT No.1 :- It is the fundamental principle of criminal Smt Jayalaxmi vs Suresh B K on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196355082/
3 jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.text:
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused,
the prosecution has examined one witness as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 and Ex.P2 documents.
Ex.P1 is the first information statement.
Ex.P.2 is the spot panchanama.
Ex.P.3 is further statement.
was examined as PW-1 Smt.Jayalakshmi.

She in her examination-in-chief has deposed that her marriage with accused No.1 was performed on 01-03-2017 and deposed after the marriage, accused looked after her well and deposed accused did not subjected her to any physical and mental cruelty, in demand of dowry and never abused, assaulted and threatened to kill her. PW-1
deposed that there was petty quarrel between her and accused in respect to family issues, for which she went to the police station.
There the police have took her signatures on documents.
PW-1 identified Ex.P.1 first information statement and also identified her signature at Ex.P1.
PW-1 also identified Ex.P.2 spot Panchanama and her signature at Ex.P2 and she pleaded her ignorance about the contents of Ex.P.1 and P.2.
The learned Sr.APP treated PW-1 as hostile witness and cross examined her.
During which PW-1 admitted that she and accused have compromised the matter and denied all other suggestions.

11. On appreciation of entire materials on record, it is apparent that PW-1 being the informant, key and material witness Smt Jayalaxmi vs Suresh B K on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196355082/
4 have turned hostile to the prosecution case.

entities.text: Smt Jayalaxmi vs Suresh B K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this court  6  C.C.No.39164/2024 was pleased to reject the prayer of the learned Sr.APP to summon other chargesheeted witnesses.

Even, if the summons was issued to other chargesheeted witnesses, no purpose would be served as the material witness has given go-bye to her own statement and also the valuable time of the court would be saved.
As such other charge sheeted witnesses were dropped and prosecution evidence was taken as closed.

In view of the material witness, turning hostile,
and in the absence of evidence of material witness, the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

12. POINT No.2:- For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER

In exercise of power conferred Under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., Accused No.1 is acquitted of the offences punishable U/s. 498A, 323 of IPC. & Sec.3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act The bail bonds of accused No.1 shall be in force for a period of 6 months.
